checks.why: a route table writes its pattern without the leading slash and names the view as a module attribute; a test that requests the URL reaches the view and what it calls
the same join lands on the view itself, and only from the URL its <int:pk> accepts: /orders/archive/ is no integer and /orders/settings/ is its own route
a view under a library decorator is still the def its route dispatches to
a class-based view routed with .as_view() is reached through its verb handler, by the one test that requests its URL
a view in a table that include() mounts is served under the mounting prefix: the test that requests /api/v1/status/ reaches it, and one requesting the bare pattern /status/ does not
what a URL runs: the view the engine says is served at a path only an include() prefix composes, and never the test that requests that path
CONTROL: /status/ is a pattern of a mounted table and a URL a test requests, but no route serves it: neither the table module nor the requesting test is said to serve it
run: what runs for a GET of /status/
